feed.title: Below the Surface

bullets: Wreck penetration is a planning problem first, a buoyancy problem second — internalizing this shifts decision-making toward safer, more predictable outcomes.
Silt-out from poor finning technique kills more divers in wrecks than equipment failures, making technique a primary safety factor.
Erosion on a wreck site changes the dive every season, requiring updated planning and adaptation to avoid unexpected hazards.
Dive planning and wreck diving intersect through the framing of safety stops: DAN's safety stops aren't suggestions but critical tradeoffs in risk management.
GoPro adoption in team dives makes the trade-off between documentation and situational awareness visible — the framing reveals the underlying decisions.
Soil erosion and site changes create second-order effects that most divers overlook, yet they fundamentally alter dive dynamics and navigation.
The key to effective wreck diving lies in running one idea for two weeks — testing decisions in practice to refine them through iteration.
When teams use GoPro, the trade-off between recording and awareness becomes explicit — the framing determines which decisions are prioritized.
